title: Guneku's medical school rewards its four best HND students
excerpt: After their HND results, the medical school based in Guneku awarded 50,000 FCFA each to its four best-performing students. Three of its HND graduates spoke about their training in a Fondom Studios feature.
sourceNote: Written fresh on 17 October 2026 from the Fondom Studios feature published on Facebook on 12 September 2026 and its caption. The feature calls the school Medvisac; the Fondom's records call it MEDPHISATG, a spelling they already note as unsettled. The award recipients and the three graduates are not named in the caption, and none is named here.
body:
In recognition of academic excellence, the medical school based in Guneku awarded 50,000 FCFA each to its four best-performing students following their Higher National Diploma (HND) results.

The awards were reported in a feature by Fondom Studios, published on 12 September 2026, ahead of the Guneku Education & Scholarship Day selection examination. In it:

  • Three students who obtained their HNDs talk about their experience and what their training has meant to them.
  • Dr. Billy Wembe, a doctor at Guneku Medical Center — which also gives students an important practical training environment — speaks on the importance of education.
  • The school's director, Prof. Dr. Tah Thierry, speaks about paying attention to students' careers and preparing them for the future.
  • HRH Dr. Fomuki Ticha IX, Fon of Guneku and patron of the scholarship initiative, speaks about supporting education in the community.

On the school's name

The feature calls the school Medvisac. The Fondom's records know it as MEDPHISATG, also written Medphisatag, and the correct form is not yet settled. It is recorded here as the feature names it.

More on the scholarship programme: Guneku Education & Scholarship Day 2026.

Source

Fondom Studios, feature of 12 September 2026. Watch it on Facebook.
